notes:
Summary: Apex is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to replace partially internal endpoints for latency-sensitive AdTech inference. Primary drivers: stable latency during auctions, predictable monthly cost, and audit/compliance for EU/NA ad data. They need a committed reserved model that covers peak auction bursts but is cost-effective given diurnal usage.

Use-case details: chat assistant for sales ops (low qps, tighter latency for agent UX), embeddings for semantic matching (high throughput batch jobs), real-time reranking inside bidding pipeline (hard SLOs - p95 vs p99 matter).

Throughput & SLO targets (customer stated):
- Aggregate throughput target: ~12k tokens/sec sustained across fleet during peak windows (~30 min bursts).
- Chat latency SLO: p95 <= 150ms for 2k concurrent user streams (short context ~512 tokens).
- Reranker latency SLO: p95 <= 80ms, p99 <= 250ms (must be bounded for auction loop).

Commit scenarios evaluated in workshop (see Drive calc):
- Scenario A (conservative): Reserve 8 x A100-80GB equiv. Baseline price assumed in model: $X/hour per GPU. Assumed utilization 65% (expected after autoscale + prefix caching). Effective unit economics: modeled $0.00035 - $0.00048 per token for chat path (varies with quantization and KV cache hit rate).
- Scenario B (balanced): Reserve 16 x A10G equiv for higher concurrency/throughput. Assumed utilization 75-80% under sustained load. Unit cost drops ~25% vs A100 scenario on tokens/sec basis for embeddings-heavy work.
- Scenario C (aggressive): 32 x mixed GPUs with burst pool. Higher committed cost but supports peak 20k tokens/sec and gives lower per-token price if utilization > 80%. Requires longer commitment (12-24mo) to realize discounts.

Key cost drivers called out: batching efficiency, KV cache hit rate, model selection (70B vs 13B quantized), and sequence length distribution. We highlighted Redwood Optimize suggestions: aggressive prefix caching for reranker, mixed model routing (13B quantized for rerank, 70B for high-fidelity chat) to control unit economics.

SLA & procurement negotiation notes:
- Apex requires explicit latency SLOs for p95/p99 with credits for missed windows; wants maintenance windows limited to quarterly and advance notice of 14 days.
- Legal pushing for data residency guarantees (EU tenant separation) and KMS integration for customer keys.
- Requested draft SOW with penalty schedule for sustained latency degradation (>3 violations/month). Redwood legal to provide template.

POC plan & measurement approach:
- 2-week dedicated POC: run synthetic auction traces + production replay (sanitized) under realistic traffic mix. Measure token/sec, p95/p99 latencies, and sustained utilization over diurnal pattern.
- Deliverables: throughput report, cost-per-token extrapolation (3 commit scenarios), recommended reserved sizing and autoscale policy, and SLA draft.

Open questions / action items:
- Apex to provide 7-day production telemetry (token counts, sequence length histogram) to refine utilization assumptions (owner: Apex infra).
- Sales/SE to produce finalized 12-month commit pricing sheet and tiered latency credits (owner: Jordan + Marcus).
- Security to confirm KMS/HSM integration timeline (ticket SEC-1127).
- Procurement requested total cost of ownership comparison vs internal self-host (due 2026-03-20).

Quotes & paraphrase from calls: "If we can't guarantee p95 for reranker, auctions break — need hard SLAs" (SRE lead). "We can trade-off some spend for a burst pool rather than oversizing committed baseline" (Head of ML).
